title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android: Interpreter agent for real-time meeting translation
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, room entitlement and meeting-policy commands are supported, and it explicitly reports Microsoft's conflicting Android support statements. Two minor qualifications remain: other Microsoft documentation gives a different voice-simulation default and announces additional language support.

claims.claim: Interpreter translates Teams meetings in real time so participants can listen in their chosen language.
claims.quote: The Interpreter agent acts as a translator in Microsoft Teams meetings, allowing participants to listen to the meeting in their chosen language with real-time translation

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: An Android release-notes entry fixes Interpreter appearing on the in-meeting console despite a disabled Interpreter policy.
claims.quote: Resolved an issue where Interpreter was shown on the in-meeting console despite the interpreter policy being set to disabled.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Interpreter performs speech-to-speech translation, producing translated speech on participants' behalf.
claims.quote: Interpreter performs real-time speech-to-speech (STS) translation using Azure Cognitive Services, supporting multi-speaker, mixed-language conversations in Teams meetings.

claims.claim: The Interpreter admin page lists Chinese (Mandarin), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish for speaking and listening.
claims.quote: Interpreter supports the following languages for speaking and listening: Chinese (Mandarin), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish.
claims.fix: After the language list, add: 'Microsoft's Teams admin release notes for May 20, 2026 also say Traditional Chinese is officially supported.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/officeupdates/teams-admin#may-20,-2026, which states 'Traditional Chinese is now officially supported.'

claims.claim: Participants can choose a simulated personal voice or a preset automated voice.
claims.quote: participants can choose to have Interpreter **simulate their own voice** when translating to others or select one of the following **preset automated voices**: Ava (female), Andrew (male), Fable Turbo (neutral).

claims.claim: Ava is the default when an automated voice is selected.
claims.quote: If an automated voice is selected, **Ava is the default.**

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table and notes
claims.claim: An administrative UI for the voice-simulation policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Interpreter" "Teams admin center" "AIInterpreter" "VoiceSimulationInInterpreter". Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/interpreter-agent-teams, which requires PowerShell for organization-wide management and gives only PowerShell policy controls.

claims.claim: Voice simulation is enabled by default, so translated speech uses the simulated personal voice unless changed.
claims.quote: **Enabled**: Sets the default value for **Choose your voice when interpreted** to **Simulate my voice**.
claims.fix: Add: 'The Interpreter admin page says voice simulation defaults to Enabled, but the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference lists Disabled as the default for VoiceSimulationInInterpreter; check the assigned policy.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps, whose parameter table says 'Default value: Disabled'.

claims.claim: VoiceSimulationInInterpreter Disabled sets the default to Automated voice without removing the simulation option.
claims.quote: **Disabled**: Sets the default value for **Choose your voice when interpreted** to **Automated voice**.

claims.claim: The voice-simulation setting applies only to simultaneous interpretation.
claims.quote: The voice simulation setting and the calling policy settings below apply only to simultaneous interpretation.

claims.claim: Voice samples and biometric data are never stored during voice simulation.
claims.quote: **Voice samples or biometric data are never stored.**
